hypothesis: If the Glacial period was at least partly simultaneous worldwide, then globally distributed benthic d18O records must show the same glacial maxima at the same ages across ocean basins.
pass_criterion: In the LR04 stack (age, d18O), each of the glacial stages MIS 2, 6, 8, 10 and 12 shows d18O at least 0.5 per mil above the mean of the adjacent interglacials, and the median absolute inter-basin lag (Atlantic vs Pacific records) in glacial maxima across the last 0.9 Myr is no more than 4 kyr.
fail_criterion: The median absolute inter-basin lag at glacial maxima exceeds 8 kyr, or fewer than 3 of the 5 named stages show a d18O excursion of at least 0.5 per mil in the stack.
interpretation: Darwin's Glacial period is mapped to Pleistocene glacial stages (marine isotope stages). His claim that global temperature was simultaneously cooler is mapped to synchronous increases in benthic foraminiferal d18O. Modern reinterpretation: d18O mixes ice volume and deep-water temperature, so it is a proxy for global cooling rather than a direct temperature measure. The stack is orbitally tuned, so lags below a few kyr cannot be resolved. His wording about belts from pole to pole is tested only as coherence across ocean basins and latitudes.

dataset.name: A Pliocene-Pleistocene stack of 57 globally distributed benthic d18O records (LR04 Stack)
dataset.publisher: PANGAEA (data from Lisiecki and Raymo, 2005, Paleoceanography)
dataset.why_it_fits: The LR04 stack combines 57 benthic d18O records from the Atlantic, Pacific and Indian Oceans, and gives age and d18O per time step. These fields let us check that glacial maxima occur at the same ages worldwide and measure their amplitudes.
